label: 100m-t9-nopcheck-j16
verdict: REJECTED: replacing the writer's six-condition per-row fence with a packet-granularity fence changed nothing (rows 10.51 -> 10.68 s, wall 50.48 -> 49.89 s; both within noise, and the SHA pins still matched).
conclusion: The 98 ns/row in the writer is run bookkeeping (compare byte, extend run, close run), not validation. At 100 MB the writer is not the pacer either: its own work is 19.5 s of a 50.5 s build and it is read-blocked 37.7 s, so the m20 context feed still paces this rung.
next: T5 (m20 counts from row contiguity) is the right 100 MB ticket; the writer's own 19.5 s/100 MB argues against T7/T8 at this rung until the context is fixed.
